> Part of the [OrgComp Training Program](index.html) — **companion material for
> the OrgComp book series, not part of any governance engine.**

These rubrics score the [Track A capstone](compliance-track.html#capstone-the-eight-slot-walk):
one document covering all eight evidence slots, backed by a real
`<engine> oscal ksi-ar` run (`<engine>` is a substitution token — see the
[tooling note](index.html#tooling-stack)). Self-assess or peer-assess; the
rubric language is deliberately the language an assessor would use.

## The scale (applies to every slot)

| Level | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Missing | Slot not addressed, or addressed without reference to the books or the mapping YAML |
| 1 | Named | Feeding books and KSI category named correctly, but controls or evidence flow are wrong/absent |
| 2 | Traced | Book → NIST anchor → KSI category → evidence source chain is complete and correct against the slot mapping |
| 3 | Assessor-ready | Level 2 **plus** a real verdict from `<engine> oscal ksi-ar`, an honest gap statement for anything not-evaluated, and the deadline that gap answers to |

**Pass bar for Track A:** every slot at level 2 or higher, **and** at least
three slots at level 3. (All eight at level 3 is the "distinguished"
outcome — it is, in substance, a ConMon narrative.)

![Figure 1 — The rubric ladder: Missing → Named → Traced → Assessor-ready, with the pass bar and the four common checks.](figs/tp-fig-04-rubric-ladder.png){fig-alt="Track A rubric ladder: levels zero through three with the pass bar"}

## Common checks (scored once, apply to the whole capstone)

| Check | Yes/No |
|---|---|
| The `ksi-ar` output file is attached/linked, not just described | |
| Every control ID cited appears in the slot mapping or the book itself (no invented controls) | |
| Scaffold/not-evaluated rules are stated as gaps, not glossed as satisfied | |
| Each gap names its forcing deadline (e.g., BOD 26-04 Dec 7 2026; 20x mandatory Jan 1 2027) | |

## Slot 1 — identity (KSI-IAM) {#slot-1}

| Criterion | Level 2 evidence | Level 3 adds |
|---|---|---|
| Books | 03, 04, 06, 07, 10 named (08 as procedural companion) | — |
| Controls | IA-2(+1/2/11), IA-5, IA-11, AC-2(+1), AC-3, AC-5/6 family, AC-17, CA-7 mapped to the right book | Before/after table for at least one AC-6 enhancement (Book 10 style) |
| Evidence flow | Sign-in/risk logs named as the source | A privileged-role trace: PIM design → control → KSI rule → audit log entry (e.g., the [PIM lab](labs/lab-b5-pim.html) export) |

| Criterion | Level 2 evidence | Level 3 adds |

## Slot 8 — training (KSI-CED) {#slot-8}

| Criterion | Level 2 evidence | Level 3 adds |

| Books | 18 (19 as the freshness/ConMon context) | — |
| Controls | AT-2(+1/+2), AT-3(+3/+5), AT-4, CP-3, IR-2 mapped to the four training dimensions | — |
| Evidence flow | The `training-effectiveness-record` JSON named as the KSI-022 evidence contract, with the ≥95% thresholds | An actual record (lab-generated is fine) passing the PASS logic, with per-identity phishing results — aggregate-only stats score 0 here, per Book 18 |

## Beyond the rubric — post-implementation KPIs {#post-implementation-kpis}

The rubric above measures **learner competency**; these KPIs measure
whether the **implemented program is working** once the architecture is
live. Every one reads from an evidence surface a slot already binds — no
new collectors, just thresholds on artifacts the ConMon calendar
(Book 19) already keeps fresh.

| KPI | Target | Evidence surface | Slot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orphan-account rate (accounts with no authoritative SSOT record) | 0, verified each leaver-sequence run | Book 04 deprovisioning evidence + sign-in logs | 1 |
| Standing privileged assignments outside break-glass | 0 — everything else PIM-eligible | Book 10 PIM audit export (the [PIM lab](labs/lab-b5-pim.html) artifact) | 1, 5 |
| KEV remediation SLA adherence | 100% of KEV-listed CVEs closed by their BOD 22-01 due date; patch SLA ≥95% | Book 11 Defender VM / scan currency evidence | 4 |
| Training completion + phishing-click trend | Completion ≥95% per role tier; per-identity phishing click-rate declining quarter-over-quarter | Book 18 `training-effectiveness-record` JSON | 8 |
| Evidence freshness compliance | Every slot inside its Book 19 freshness rule (e.g., SBOM ≤90 days at submission) | Timestamps in the `ksi-ar` export | all |
| Satisfied-KSI trend (CA-7(3)) | Non-decreasing; any drop opens a POA&M entry automatically | Archived Assessment Results history | all |

A program can pass every capstone and still fail these — that is the
point: the rubric certifies people, the KPIs watch the system they built.
